name: Naamah, Velvet Ash Enchantress
loreTies: Naamah embodies velvet ash seduction, infernal charm, survival, and restorative darkness within The Infernal Dominion.
The Black-Iron Gate allows this deity to enter Ascension-era dungeon routes without collapsing the individuality of other Realms.
Infernal Dominion culture, symbols, weapons, and divine law shape every ability, artifact, silhouette, and combat choice.
shortBackstory: Naamah, Velvet Ash Enchantress, is a playable goddess in Mythos Gates: Ascension. Naamah is the true source-realm divinity behind the mythology — velvet ash seduction, infernal charm, survival, and restorative darkness. Ascension expands divine power during the current Gate crisis; it does not turn a mortal into a god.

chapters.title: Divine Origin
chapters.text: Naamah is not a mortal hero inspired by myth. Naamah is the actual goddess recognized by Infernal Dominion source culture, born from the supernatural laws of The Infernal Dominion. Their domain — velvet ash seduction, infernal charm, survival, and restorative darkness — determines their symbols, weapons, posture, combat instincts, and relationship to sacred authority.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Within Infernal Dominion, Naamah expresses the civilization rather than merely representing it. Their visual identity must carry the materials, beauty standards, divine symbols, and sacred rules of The Infernal Dominion. Their gameplay role, Sustain, must grow from mythology first and mechanics second.

chapters.title: Mythos Gate Wound
chapters.text: During the Ascension era, Naamah can interact with The Black-Iron Gate because divine beings are intrinsically connected to their Realms. The Gate does not become a simple teleportation portal; it is a mysterious boundary where separate mythological realities become traversable. Naamah understands some rites of crossing, but not the complete origin of the Mythos Gates.

chapters.title: Dungeon Role
chapters.text: When selected by the Avatar, Naamah enters the dungeon alone as one god or goddess against multiple enemies. No army follows. No squad shares control. Every room, trap, shrine, relic, elite, and boss encounter must test how velvet ash seduction, infernal charm, survival, and restorative darkness survives pressure from creatures, rival Realm laws, and unstable Gate conditions.

chapters.title: Ascension Conflict
chapters.text: Ascension is the current story arc, not the permanent end-state of the Mythos Gates universe. For Naamah, Ascension means restoration, awakening, evolution, or expansion of existing divine power. Their personal conflict is to recover strength without reducing Infernal Dominion mythology into raw fuel for the crisis.

relationshipHooks: Faction witnesses interpret how Naamah crosses The Black-Iron Gate.
Rival deities challenge the limits of cross-Realm travel.
Dungeon lore pickups reveal Gate mystery without resolving the full origin.
developmentStatus: Playable deity backstory aligned to Mythos Gates identity, one-deity dungeon runs, current Ascension arc, and preserved Lore Codex canon.
mythicSource: source culture humans later copied as hell, demonology, and infernal contract lore
visualCanon: Vasha is a cinder-broker of contract law. Her ash velvet, black-iron jewelry, blood-wax seals, coin-chain tools, and too-calm smile should feel like the origin of later devil-bargain folklore.
title: Velvet Ash Enchantress

mythosGatesCanon.identityRule: Naamah is the actual goddess of Infernal Dominion source mythology, never a mortal hero or generic champion.
mythosGatesCanon.arcRule: Ascension restores, awakens, evolves, or expands existing divine power; it does not make the character a god for the first time.
mythosGatesCanon.mysteryRule: The backstory may reveal how this deity interacts with the Mythos Gates, but must not resolve the full origin of the Gates.
